0.1.0.lead: nexdeck is here: a live dashboard for your homelab with thirty integrations, boards for desktop, phone and wall displays, and actions right on the cards.

sections.title: Live boards
sections.body: Values change in front of you. The server collects every service once and pushes changes to every open browser.

sections.title: Integrations
sections.body: Docker, Proxmox, Synology, Unraid, TrueNAS, Pi-hole, AdGuard, UniFi, Plex, Jellyfin, the *arr family, Home Assistant, Uptime Kuma and more.

sections.title: Wall displays
sections.body: A kiosk link shows a board without sign-in, cycles pages and dims at night.

sections.title: Notifications
sections.body: Outages and failed actions reach you via Telegram, e-mail, Web Push, ntfy, Gotify, Discord, Slack or Apprise.

small: Boards export and import as YAML, and files in data/boards provision them.
Docker labels nexdeck.* and homepage.* create tiles automatically.
Personal API tokens for scripts and automations.

0.2.0.lead: A deep read of the whole codebase, and then the repairs it found: 146 points in fourteen blocks. Nine of them were holes somebody could have walked through.

sections.title: Nine holes closed
sections.body: A board named after a number reached other people's boards. An action on a card could be anything the caller made up. A member could import a board that read the server's secret key. Uploads could run in nexdeck's own origin, and the Synology password travelled in the address.

sections.title: A way back in
sections.body: If the last administrator is locked out and there is no mail server, starting the container once with NEXDECK_RESCUE=1 prints a one-time sign-in link, good for fifteen minutes. It goes to the terminal, never to the log.

sections.title: Arrange a board without a mouse
sections.body: Arrow keys move the focused card, Shift resizes it. All three form factors follow. And while editing, the whole card is the handle: a card whose face is a link used to have nothing to take hold of but its rim.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Tab to a card

sections.title: A card that does not know a number says so
sections.body: Missing values were drawn as zero, which reads as measured and fine. Fifty-four places that compute a percentage now say they do not know instead.

small: Running nexdeck is written down: backups, restoring, updating and the Docker socket.
Seventeen settings that were documented nowhere are in the README, with a guard that keeps the table in step.
A card can no longer fall silent for good: any unexpected failure puts a message on it and tries again.
Old records are cleaned up on a schedule, and every limit has a number behind it.

0.3.0.lead: Four new cards, a place to look after the files you upload, and n8n. Nothing in the new cards is typed out in a syntax: what you can pick, you pick.

sections.title: Button card
sections.body: One card, one button. It opens a board, one page of it, or an address, chosen from a list. Three looks, and a colour if you want one; the name on that colour is black or white by measurement, not by guess.

sections.title: Pictures, uploaded or linked
sections.body: One picture or a slideshow, with an interval, a crop and captions. Upload a file, name an address, or take one out of the media you already have. Drag the handle to change the order.

sections.title: One container, all of it
sections.body: Pick a single container or virtual machine and see everything the service reports. Docker, Portainer, Synology's Container Manager and VM Manager, and Proxmox. What a service does not measure is left out rather than drawn as zero.

sections.title: Media
sections.body: Every file you have uploaded, with its size and what still shows it. Deleting one names the cards and boards that would show a placeholder afterwards. The same file uploaded twice is one file now.

small: n8n: workflows with a publish button, the last runs, and how many of them failed.
The clock has a face with hands, and a colour for the digits or the hands.
Boards are sorted by a handle, the way a list on a phone is. The same handle answers the arrow keys.
Looking for an update no longer needs the daily check to be switched on.
The Synology password stopped travelling in the address.

0.4.0.lead: Cards can be drawn as bars, a ring or a chart, media libraries can be told to look for new files, and a button can trigger it.

sections.title: A card can be drawn differently
sections.body: Bars for a list, a ring for parts of a whole, a chart for a card that measures two things. The choice sits under View in the card's settings, next to the dial. 91 list cards and 63 cards with two numbers have it.

sections.title: Charts draw every line
sections.body: A card that records WAN in and WAN out drew one of them and threw the other away. Both are drawn now, on one scale, with a legend.
sections.path: Edit mode > gear > View > A chart

sections.title: Look for new files
sections.body: Plex, Jellyfin and Emby have a Libraries card with a button that asks the server to scan. Per library on Plex; on Jellyfin and Emby only all of them, because that is the only thing that works there.
sections.path: Edit mode > Add widget > Plex, Jellyfin or Emby > Libraries

sections.title: A button that does something
sections.body: The button card has a third kind: trigger an action. Pick the connection, what it offers and what it acts on, all three from lists. Nothing is typed.
sections.path: Edit mode > Add widget > Basics > Button card

sections.title: Plex server load as a dial
sections.body: Four percentages, and a dial shows one, so the settings ask which: Plex's processor or memory, or the host's.
sections.path: Edit mode > gear > View > A dial

sections.title: Synology virtual machines, measured right
sections.body: The memory of a guest was divided by what it was assigned instead of by the host's, so a healthy machine reported 102% full, and the processor load was shown ten times too high. Both now match what the Virtual Machine Manager says.
sections.path: Edit mode > Add widget > Synology DSM

small: A card that is drawn as a ring keeps its own headline in the middle, and every slice is named: a colour is not a label.
The Synology machine picker offered Docker containers, and picking one answered that there was no such machine. Two cards, two lists.
Proxmox with a token that sees no node said so instead of reporting nought guests on nought nodes.
A Speedtest Tracker that has not measured yet tests green: the old test asked for a result that a fresh install does not have and blamed the address.
UniFi's switch card had no demo data of its own and quietly showed the console summary instead.
A change saved in a card's settings stopped jumping back to the old one until the page was reloaded.

0.5.0.lead: A card can have a field you type into, MeTube is the first to use one, and a finished download can be saved to the machine you are sitting at.

sections.title: Fetch a video by pasting its address
sections.body: A card with a text field and a button. Paste a video address, press, and MeTube fetches the file. Video or audio only, and the quality is yours to pick.
sections.path: Edit mode > Add widget > MeTube > Fetch a video

sections.title: A card may leave one blank for you to fill in
sections.body: Everything nexdeck runs is picked from a list a service handed over, and that is what keeps a card from being a way in. A field is the exception, so the adapter has to declare it: which single parameter is blank, and what may go in it. An address is checked the way every address you type into nexdeck is checked.
sections.path: Edit mode > Add widget > MeTube > Fetch a video

sections.title: Save a download to your own machine
sections.body: MeTube fetches to the server, which is where the file then sits. A finished row now has a save button beside its bin, and the file comes through nexdeck, so it works from outside the house and really saves instead of playing in a tab.
sections.path: Edit mode > Add widget > MeTube > Downloads

sections.title: A chart of what a card kept itself
sections.body: Speedtest Tracker keeps months of measurements, and nexdeck only ever drew its own day. Its History card asks the tracker instead: 24 hours, 7, 30 or 90 days, download, upload or both, as a line or as bars.
sections.path: Edit mode > Add widget > Speedtest Tracker > History

sections.title: Three services leave beta
sections.body: Proxmox VE, Speedtest Tracker and Immich, all three confirmed against live instances.

small: A setting made in a card no longer shows, jumps back to the old one, and needs a reload to stick.
The button for looking for new files was a grey box: its symbol was never in the set the app bundles. Every symbol on every button is now checked.
A failed speedtest is drawn as a gap in the line rather than as a dip to nought, which would be an outage that never happened.
A button says what it did in the language the board is in.

0.5.1.lead: One fix, and it took three tries to find: a change made in a card could still jump back to what it was.

sections.title: A setting stays put
sections.body: Two roads carry the same card to your browser, and they do not arrive in order. Saving sent the new answer straight away, and a board request that had gone out just before the save came back afterwards with the state from before it, overwriting the fresh one. On a card that is read every few seconds you would never notice; on a clock, whose next reading is an hour away, the old setting stayed until you reloaded. An answer older than the one on screen is now turned away.

small: A card's own answer can no longer be overtaken by one that was already being fetched when you saved.
A saved card keeps what you saved until the board really carries it, rather than until any request comes back.

0.5.2.lead: Three fixes, and two of them are the same fault wearing different clothes: the server was doing a slow piece of work in the one place where nothing else can happen while it runs.

sections.title: A new board fills in seconds, not in a quarter of a minute
sections.body: Every service logo on a card is fetched by the server and kept on disk, and a brand new installation has nothing kept yet, so the first board asks for a dozen at once. For each of them the server built a fresh connection from scratch, which costs about a second of pure work, and it did that work where nothing else could get a turn. Measured in a browser: the board answer that carries the first data of every card used to come back after fourteen seconds. It comes back after five now. What you saw before was a board of cards that stayed empty for a while, and a button card that led nowhere until it filled in.

sections.title: Save no longer misses
sections.body: A message appears in the bottom right corner and stays for five seconds, and that is exactly where a settings sheet keeps its Save button. A press meant for Save landed on the message instead, so nothing happened and pressing again did not help either. Messages let presses through now; only their own close button still takes one.

small: A notification, a web push, a sign-in through your identity provider and the look for a newer version no longer hold the whole server up for about a second each.
Someone with a phone, a tablet and two browsers used to pay that second four times over for a single notification.

0.6.0.lead: Nexview requests can be approved right from the board, with a choice of folder and profile where one is needed.

sections.title: Approve Nexview requests from the board
sections.body: A new Nexview card lists what waits for approval, with its cover and who asked for it. One press approves or turns it down.
sections.path: Edit mode > Add widget > Nexview > Requests to approve

sections.title: A choice where one is needed
sections.body: When a request still needs a target folder or a quality profile, Approve opens a short sheet with the folders and profiles of that request's own Radarr or Sonarr. A list of several never starts on its first entry, so nothing lands in a folder nobody picked.

sections.title: Only with a key that may approve
sections.body: The buttons appear only when the Nexview key may decide. With a read-only key the requests are listed without them and the card says why; the connection test says so when you set it up.

small: The buttons of the approval card show without hovering, so they can be reached on a touchscreen.
The board and the wall display ask the same question before an action runs.

0.6.1.lead: One fix: covers on the Nexview approval card show again.

sections.title: Covers are back
sections.body: The poster of a waiting request did not load on a board the app's offline helper was looking after. That helper now leaves pictures from other addresses to the browser, and the cover appears.

small: A test now loads a picture from another address on a page the offline helper looks after, so this cannot come back unnoticed.

0.6.2.lead: Your phone now shows the board in the order you arranged it.

sections.title: One arrangement for every screen
sections.body: Arrange a board once on a wide screen. A tablet or a wall display shows exactly that arrangement, and a phone stacks the cards in the same order: row by row, left to right, lists at the full width and small tiles in pairs.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) on a wide screen

small: In edit mode on a phone the cards stay put, and a note says that they are arranged on a wider screen.
Arrangements made for the phone or the tablet before this version are no longer used.
A new demo board comes with its arrangement again, instead of every card at the same size in the order it was made.

0.7.0.lead: Six new integrations: Cup, Healthchecks, ChangeDetection.io, Miniflux, autobrr and Firefly III.

sections.title: Container updates with Cup
sections.body: See which images have a newer version waiting, the biggest step first, and make Cup check again with one press.

sections.title: Cron jobs with Healthchecks
sections.body: Down and late checks come first, from your own instance or from healthchecks.io.

sections.title: Web pages, feeds, releases and money
sections.body: ChangeDetection.io shows what changed, Miniflux what is unread, autobrr what was grabbed, and Firefly III your net worth, subscriptions and budgets.

small: All six were measured against running instances and start without the beta badge.
Healthchecks closes its connections after every answer; nexdeck asks for exactly that, so no card loses a request.

0.8.0.lead: Eight new integrations: Gitea, Forgejo, CrowdSec, Semaphore UI, Karakeep, Mealie, Kopia and Duplicati.

sections.title: Backups with Kopia and Duplicati
sections.body: Every snapshot source or backup job with its last good run, and a failed one on top with the reason. Duplicati also shows which job is running.

sections.title: Your Git server
sections.body: Gitea and Forgejo show open issues or pull requests and the latest Actions jobs, red ones marked. Semaphore UI shows how every template last ended.
sections.path: Settings > Integrations > Gitea, Forgejo or Semaphore UI

sections.title: Blocked addresses, bookmarks and the kitchen
sections.body: CrowdSec shows what it blocks right now, Karakeep what is still waiting to be read, and Mealie the meal plan and the shopping list.

small: All eight were measured against running instances and start without the beta badge.
A Duplicati job that failed once and ran fine since no longer counts as failed, although Duplicati still keeps the old error.
"Failed" reads "Fehlgeschlagen" in German now.

0.9.0.lead: Six new integrations: Vikunja, Kimai, Grocy, Shlink, Meilisearch and Linkwarden.

sections.title: Tasks and time with Vikunja and Kimai
sections.body: Vikunja shows what is overdue and due today across every project. Kimai shows the running timer and the hours booked this week, and the timer can be stopped from the card.

sections.title: The pantry with Grocy
sections.body: What expired, is overdue or due soon, and what fell below its minimum stock.

sections.title: Short URLs, search and links
sections.body: Shlink shows visits and which short URLs no longer redirect, Meilisearch the documents of each index and failed indexing, Linkwarden the links saved last.

small: All six were measured against running instances and start without the beta badge.
For Vikunja, what counts as today follows the time zone set on the integration, because an API token cannot read the user's own.
Buttons on the rows of the n8n and Synology cards were refused when pressed; they work again.

0.10.0.lead: Five new integrations: RomM, NetBox, Dawarich, wger and wg-easy.

sections.title: Your network with NetBox and wg-easy
sections.body: NetBox shows the devices that are not active and how full each prefix is. wg-easy shows which WireGuard clients are connected and how much went through.

sections.title: Distance and weight with Dawarich and wger
sections.body: Dawarich shows the kilometres of this month and this year and warns when your phone stopped sending points. wger shows your weight and how it changed over 30 days.

sections.title: The game library with RomM
sections.body: Every platform with its number of games, and the games added last.

small: All five were measured against running instances and start without the beta badge.
ArchiveBox stays on the list: its stable release has no API yet.

0.11.0.lead: Your music in nexdeck: a player card plays the library of Plex, Jellyfin or Emby in the browser.

sections.title: Play the music library
sections.body: The card shows the newest albums, albums, artists, playlists, a search and the queue, with the cover filling the card. The music keeps playing when you switch boards, and nothing is reported to the server.
sections.path: Edit mode > Add widget > Plex, Jellyfin or Emby > Music player

sections.title: A bar, a round button or the top bar
sections.body: When the card is out of sight a floating bar takes over. Drag it into a corner, fold it into a round button, or put the player into the top bar.

sections.title: Edit playlists
sections.body: Make a playlist from a track, an album or the whole queue, add and take out tracks, rename and delete. Smart playlists on Plex stay as they are.

small: Sound quality per browser: the original, 320 or 128 kbit/s, lowered by itself when a track keeps stalling.
Somebody who may only look sees the card without buttons; a kiosk plays only when its link allows actions.
0.9.0 and 0.10.0 were not published on their own. Their eleven integrations arrive with this version, from Vikunja to wg-easy.

0.11.1.lead: Two fixes: a wall display's link no longer locks you out, and Reolink devices stop running out of sessions.

sections.title: Kiosk links in your own browser
sections.body: Opening a wall display's link in your own browser left a cookie that shut you out of every other board. Your account and the display now each count for what they allow.

sections.title: Reolink keeps letting nexdeck in
sections.body: Cards starting together, the Test button and saving a connection each opened a session at the device and never closed it, until the device refused with too many users. Every session is handed back now.

small: A Reolink device that refuses logins right now lets nexdeck in again once its old sessions expire, at most an hour after updating.

0.12.0.lead: 20 new integrations, from Backrest to Zabbix.

sections.title: Hosts and containers
sections.body: What's Up Docker and Watchtower show which containers wait for an update and start it from the card. Komodo shows your stacks, Backrest your backup plans, Netdata and Zabbix alerts and open problems, Ollama and Open WebUI the loaded models and who uses them.
sections.path: Settings > Integrations > Backrest, Komodo, Netdata, Ollama, Open WebUI, Watchtower, What's Up Docker or Zabbix

sections.title: Network and monitoring
sections.body: Gatus shows which endpoints are down, Blocky how much it blocks with a five-minute pause, NetAlertX new devices on the network, and Pocket ID who signed in lately.
sections.path: Settings > Integrations > Blocky, Gatus, NetAlertX or Pocket ID

sections.title: Media
sections.body: Sportarr shows the sports events of the next days and the ones still missing, Tube Archivist its download queue and archive.
sections.path: Settings > Integrations > Sportarr or Tube Archivist

sections.title: Home and files
sections.body: Tandoor Recipes brings the meal plan and the shopping list, Homebox the inventory and its warranties, Wallos the next payments, Ghostfolio the portfolio, PhotoPrism and BookOrbit your photos and books.
sections.path: Settings > Integrations > BookOrbit, Ghostfolio, Homebox, PhotoPrism, Tandoor Recipes or Wallos

small: Every one of them was measured against a running instance before it was written, so none carries the beta badge.

0.12.1.lead: Buttons and fields look the way they were drawn again.

sections.title: Flat buttons on the cards
sections.body: Refresh, link, settings and remove sat in a frame on every card and were a third larger than drawn. They are small flat icons again, and so are the close buttons in dialogs and the buttons in the notices.

sections.title: Password fields
sections.body: A long password ran under the button that shows it. The text now stops before the button.

small: Sizes, borders and colors given to single elements apply again, 90 in all: among them the sign-in buttons, the round wake button, the tab bar on a phone and the warning on the backups page.

0.13.0.lead: This version closes gaps and fixes faults, and a few things work differently than before.

sections.title: Apprise only for administrators
sections.body: Members no longer see Apprise among the notification channels, and an Apprise channel a member set up earlier stops sending. Apprise follows redirects in its own library, where nexdeck's address check does not reach.

sections.title: Wall displays keep their token
sections.body: After the first load the address of a kiosk display shows only /k, and a reload comes back in by itself. Displays already on the wall move over at their next load. A revoked kiosk link cuts off an open display's live data within 25 seconds.

sections.title: Refresh now
sections.body: A second press within five seconds shows the answer of the first instead of asking the service again.

sections.title: Public URL
sections.body: The address set here now counts for Web Push and the rescue link as well. NEXDECK_URL_BASE is gone: the interface never ran below a sub path, so an installation that set it runs under / again.

small: Uploaded pictures load only for signed-in accounts and kiosk displays.
Connections no longer pass cookies on to each other.
Messages on a live board close by themselves again, and this window closes at once.
The problems card names tiles whose reachability check fails.
A backup leaves the chart history out.
The test button of a notification channel takes five presses in ten minutes.

0.14.0.lead: Two things asked for on GitHub: Nomad, and somewhere to put Frigate's credentials.

sections.title: Nomad
sections.body: HashiCorp's orchestrator now has three cards. Jobs lists every job of a namespace with its state and how many allocations run, the troubled ones first; Nodes shows the clients with their state and how much of each is allocated; Cluster is the same counts as one number. A job can be stopped from its row, and a service job's task group scaled up or down by one, which is what a job that should only run when it is needed asks for. A cluster without ACLs needs no credentials.

sections.title: Frigate takes a user and a password
sections.body: Frigate answers on two ports: 5000 is its internal API and needs no account, 8971 is the authenticated one and is what a reverse proxy in front of it uses. The card only had an address, so anything but port 5000 refused it with nowhere to put an account. It signs in now and carries the token Frigate hands out. A viewer account is enough.

sections.title: What a Nomad node shows is allocated, not used
sections.body: Nomad's server API carries no live load; that sits behind every client on its own. The card adds up what the allocations reserved instead, and where the token may read a single namespace it shows no share at all rather than that namespace's share of a node.

small: Scaling a Nomad task group reads the count from the cluster at the moment the button is pressed, so a group whose allocation has died is not counted down from nothing.
The Frigate connection test counts cameras the way the cards do; it counted the detection rate as a camera.
A Frigate sign-in that was turned down is not tried again for a minute, because Frigate limits failed logins per address.

0.14.1.lead: Three integrations that answered wrongly, all reported on GitHub.

sections.title: TrueNAS with a read-only key
sections.body: On TrueNAS 25.04 and later the old REST API turns a Read-Only Administrator's key away, so the cards needed a full administrator. With an https:// address nexdeck now uses TrueNAS' current API, where that key reads the system, the pools and the alerts. Over http:// the key stays on the old API, because TrueNAS revokes a key for good once it arrives over a plain connection; the message then says to switch to https.

sections.title: Jellystat's most watched titles
sections.body: The card came back with an error on current Jellystat versions, which want to know whether films, shows or music are meant. It has a choice for that now; by default it shows all three, each row marked with its kind.

small: The pfSense connection test no longer fails with a 404 while the cards work.
The pfSense system card shows the temperature instead of a question mark.
TrueNAS alerts show the day they were raised instead of a long number.

0.14.2.lead: Unraid keeps its cards when one part cannot be read, and TrueNAS leaves beta.

sections.title: Unraid shows what it can
sections.body: When Unraid refused one part of what the cards read, a switched-off VM service for instance, or a key without permission for Docker, every Unraid card showed the same error. Each part is now read on its own. A part that fails leaves a question mark where it belonged, and the connection test names what it could not read.

small: TrueNAS is out of beta: every card was run against a real TrueNAS 25.10.

0.15.0.lead: nexmail joins the board: unread mail per mailbox, and the latest senders and subjects.

sections.title: Unread mail
sections.body: The total in the inbox and one row per mailbox under it. A mailbox whose mail server rejects the stored password turns red, because its number is from before.

sections.title: Latest mail
sections.body: Sender and subject of the newest messages, unread ones in bold, and each row opens the message in nexmail. It needs a key that may read sender and subject; for a key that may only count, the library says so instead of adding the card.

small: Both cards pick their mailboxes from the ones shared on the key, all of them by default.
nexmail needs version 0.17.0 or newer, and its operator has to allow API keys first.

0.15.1.lead: Fixes from the GitHub issues of the last days, new Frigate cards, and a board that says when it shows invented data.

sections.title: Frigate shows your cameras
sections.body: On current Frigate versions the cameras card listed two entries of Frigate's statistics as cameras at 0 fps and missed the real ones, and every detection read 0%. Both read the current answers now. New from the same issue: a camera's latest picture, detections with their thumbnails, today's detections by kind, and a health card that stays empty while everything runs.

sections.title: Demo mode says so
sections.body: With the demo board from the first start, every connection shows invented data, also the ones you add later. The board now says so while demo mode is on, and the connection test adds that the cards will not show what it just found.
sections.path: System > Integrations > Demo mode for everything

sections.title: Nomad counts what fails now
sections.body: Nomad keeps failed allocations in its job summary as a tally that never goes down, so healthy jobs showed red. The jobs and cluster cards now count only failed allocations that still stand.

small: Radarr's upcoming card shows the next of a film's release dates and names its kind, not a digital release that has passed.
On cards three rows tall and up, the row of small figures wraps onto a second line instead of scrolling sideways.
The setup wizard names the right place to switch demo mode off.

0.16.0.lead: nexpulse joins the board: your speed tests, their history, latency under load, and a button to test now.

sections.title: Latest result and a button to test
sections.body: Download, upload, ping and jitter of the newest test, a running test live as it happens, and yellow when nexpulse finds the line below your plan. With a key that may start tests, a button runs one; a button card can do the same.

sections.title: History, summary and recent tests
sections.body: Download and upload or the ping over up to 90 days, with a failed test drawn as a gap. The summary shows average, median, lowest or highest and how often a test failed or fell below the plan; the list shows the newest tests, failed ones red.

sections.title: Latency under load
sections.body: How much the ping grows while the line is busy, graded A+ to F on the steps of the Waveform bufferbloat test.

small: nexpulse 0.1.1 or newer tells nexdeck what a key may do. On 0.1.0 the button is always shown, and a key that may only read is told so when it presses it.
A button pointed at an action that needs no target says so, instead of a yellow "offers nothing".

0.16.1.lead: TrueNAS: nexdeck no longer uses the old REST API where TrueNAS has deprecated it, so the alert about it on the NAS goes away.

sections.title: No more "Deprecated REST API usage" on TrueNAS
sections.body: With an http:// address and a full administrator's key, or behind a reverse proxy that does not pass WebSockets on, nexdeck read TrueNAS through its old REST API. TrueNAS 25.10 counts every such call and shows an alert with the number of the last 24 hours, and TrueNAS 26 removes that API. nexdeck now checks without the key whether TrueNAS has the current API, and then sends nothing over the old one. The card says what to change: https:// in the address, or WebSockets in the proxy. A TrueNAS before 25.04 keeps its cards as they were.

small: Measured on a real TrueNAS 25.10.7: eight reads by the cards showed up on the NAS as "8 times", and with this version the count stays where it is.
If something in front of TrueNAS answers 404 in its place, the version TrueNAS reports decides, asked once an hour.

0.17.0.lead: Boards you can shape: templates, an import from Homepage or Homarr, finer grids, colour themes, and a wall tablet that signs itself in at home.

sections.title: Start from a template or bring your old dashboard
sections.body: Six ready-made boards, from a homelab overview to a wall display that fits the screen. Each asks which of your connections fills its slots and leaves out what you do not run. Or paste the files of Homepage or Homarr: you see a plan of pages, connections and cards first, and nothing is made before you confirm it.

sections.title: Finer grids and arranging by the handful
sections.body: A board can have 12, 24 or 36 columns, be drawn wide or across the whole screen, and fit its rows to the window. In edit mode, Shift or Ctrl and a click select several cards to move together; Close gaps, undo and redo, four named sizes per card, and sending cards to another page or board.

sections.title: Signed in on the home network
sections.body: For a wall tablet: name your home networks and one ordinary account, and a browser there is signed in without a password. Never an administrator, and the session opens nothing outside the home network. Behind a reverse proxy, name it in NEXDECK_TRUSTED_PROXIES first; the page shows what nexdeck makes of your own address.

sections.title: Colour themes
sections.body: Seven themes of nexdeck's own, each for dark and light, or any other pasted in as JSON. A pasted theme is told which colours are too weak to read before it is saved.

sections.title: nexcrate and more GitHub
sections.body: nexcrate joins with eight cards, paired with a code shown in both apps. GitHub gains issues and pull requests, and workflow runs, and takes an optional token for private repositories and a higher limit.

small: Notes are written right on the card, and a - [ ] list ticks with a touch.
TrueNAS shows CPU usage and the memory its services use, with the ZFS cache apart.
Leaving demo mode removes the invented connections, cards and boards, after asking.
Value cards draw a line under their number, and only list cards with numbers offer bars.
Frigate and GitHub are out of beta.
The image now reads forwarding headers itself (--no-proxy-headers). A compose file that overrides the command should do the same.

0.18.0.lead: Any managed switch on a board: ports, speeds, traffic and PoE, from the standard MIBs, whatever name is on the box.

sections.title: One SNMP connection for every vendor
sections.body: Cisco, HP, Aruba, Netgear, TP-Link, Zyxel, D-Link, MikroTik, Ubiquiti and the rest answer the same standard MIBs, so nexdeck reads those and nothing vendor-specific. SNMPv3 with SHA and AES is the default, SNMPv2c with a community is there for devices that have nothing else, and it says plainly that a community travels unencrypted. Read only: nexdeck never writes to a switch.

sections.title: Five cards, and findings that name the port
sections.body: The device with its model, firmware and uptime; every port with state, speed, duplex and what LLDP says hangs on it; the traffic of one port with its history, worked out from two counter readings; PoE with its budget and what is drawn; and findings: an uplink that is down, ports collecting errors, links stuck at 100 Mbit/s or in half duplex.

sections.title: A test that says what is actually wrong
sections.body: A device that stays silent over SNMPv2c gets all three causes named, because a wrong community looks exactly like a switched-off agent. Over SNMPv3 the answer is exact: this user is unknown, this authentication password is wrong, or, when the device only falls silent, that the user and password are right and the encryption is not.

small: A connection sheet can carry a short setup guide, and shows only the fields that belong to what you chose.
The search for a connection finds the vendor behind a protocol: type Cisco or Netgear and the SNMP connection comes up.

0.19.0.lead: Two more networks on the board: NetBird's peers and Pangolin's sites and resources. And four things people reported, fixed.

sections.title: NetBird
sections.body: The peers of your NetBird network, self-hosted or on NetBird Cloud: who is connected, when the others were last seen, and whose login has expired. An expired login comes first, because that peer stays cut off until somebody signs it in again. A personal access token is all it needs, best one of a service user.

sections.title: Pangolin
sections.body: Sites online or offline, and the resources Pangolin serves from them: public ones with their health, private ones with their destination. It reads the Integration API, which a self-hosted Pangolin has to switch on first; the connection sheet says how. A key that lacks one of the three permissions it needs is told which one.

sections.title: Identity providers can be changed
sections.body: A pencil next to each provider opens it in the form. Leave the secret empty to keep it, switch a provider off without removing it, and see a warning when a new short name changes the redirect URI. Until now the only way was to delete it, which let go of every linked account.

small: Sign-in through authentik without a signing key now says exactly that, instead of an error nobody could read.
The lowest card of a board can be resized in edit mode; the edit bar used to lie over its corner.
Tautulli's Most watched card shows TV shows and music as well as movies.

0.19.1.lead: Nexview's approval card is ready for the coming Nexview with nexcrate.

sections.title: Approving with nexcrate behind Nexview
sections.body: With nexcrate doing the fetching, a request has no folder and no profile to choose, and the card used to show no approve button at all. Now it approves straight away and shows the version the request asks for by name. With Radarr and Sonarr nothing changes.
sections.path: Edit mode > Add widget > Nexview > Requests to approve

small: Two tests that failed now and then under load are steady again.

0.19.2.lead: Recently added shows a series once, and covers no longer lie over each other.

sections.title: One cover per series
sections.body: Plex listed every new episode on its own, so ten new episodes of one show were ten times the same cover. A series is now one cover at the place of its newest episode, with the number of new episodes under it. A single new episode keeps its number and title. Jellyfin and Emby count their new episodes the same way.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Add widget > Plex > Recently added

small: Covers in a card too low for them keep their rows apart and the card scrolls, on every cover card.

0.19.3.lead: TCP and ping checks on an app tile reach the service when Target is left empty.

sections.title: TCP and ping checks on the tile's link
sections.body: With Target left empty, a TCP or ping check takes the tile's link, and the link is a whole address such as http://nas:7878. TCP read http://nas as the name of the machine and ping tried the whole address, so the dot stayed red for a service that was up. TCP now knocks at the host and port of the link, 80 or 443 when it names none, and ping reaches the host. Checks saved that way are right from their next run.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > settings of an app tile > Check reachability

small: The settings of an app tile show the reachability switch once, in the box of the check.

0.20.0.lead: A status page, one list of updates, the machine nexdeck runs on, your public address, the notices on the board and your YouTube subscriptions. The calendar shows times now, and a demo tile that stayed grey checks its address again.

sections.title: Status page
sections.body: Every card with a reachability check on one card: how each answered last and how fast, its availability bars and how much of the time it was up, what is down at the top. It shows this board or every board of its owner, never somebody else's.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Add widget > Basics > Status page

sections.title: One list of updates
sections.body: What has a newer version, gathered in one place: the containers What's Up Docker and Cup list, a Watchtower run that failed, the newest release of the GitHub projects you follow, and nexdeck itself. nexdeck is asked about only through the update check in System.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Add widget > Basics > Updates

sections.title: This machine
sections.body: Processor, memory, load, temperature, uptime and the disk nexdeck keeps its data on, read straight from the kernel. No agent, and in Docker nothing to mount.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Add widget > Basics > This machine

sections.title: Your public address
sections.body: The address your connection has on the internet, from ipify or ipwho.is, without an account. When it changes the card says so and keeps the address before; for a board guests see it can show the last block only.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Add widget > Public IP address

sections.title: Notices and YouTube subscriptions
sections.body: The notice centre as a card, for a wall where nobody opens the bell. And the newest videos of the channels an account follows, with a YouTube Data API key on the YouTube connection.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Add widget > Basics > Notices, or YouTube > Subscriptions

sections.title: Times in the calendar
sections.body: Appointments from iCal show their time, all-day entries first. Times from Google Calendar and other zones are placed on the server's clock, each occurrence on its own, and today's appointments leave the card once they are over.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Add widget > Calendar > Upcoming

small: App tiles from the demo board that stayed grey check their address again, and saving a tile switches its check on (issue #17).
The dot of an app tile says on hover why it is grey or red.
A percentage row in a stats card keeps its bar; Docker's CPU, counted per core, keeps its line.
TrueNAS: a key that may not read statistics no longer costs the system card five seconds on every refresh.

0.21.0.lead: nextrmnl joins the board: live SSH sessions, the latest ones and whether your connections answer. The About page names the whole nexapps family.

sections.title: nextrmnl
sections.body: Four cards from the connection manager of the nexapps family: its status, who is connected where right now, the latest sessions and how they ended, and whether each connection answers. A server that answers with another host key turns the card red. It needs nextrmnl 0.3.0 or newer and a read-only API key from there, which opens no terminal, no file and no vault.

small: The About page names nexcrate, nexbeat and nextrmnl in the family line, next to Nexview, nexmail and nexpulse.

0.22.0.lead: Arcane joins the board: every Docker environment it manages, with its projects, containers and waiting image updates, and the buttons to act on them.

sections.title: Arcane
sections.body: Five cards from the Docker manager Arcane, across the local environment and every one behind its agents: an overview, the environments and whether each answers, projects with start, stop, redeploy and update, containers with their health and start, stop and restart, and the containers with a newer image, each with a button that pulls it and recreates the container. Every card but the environments can be narrowed to one environment. A scoped API key from Arcane is enough; the connection sheet lists the permissions each card and button needs.

small: Requested in issue #18. Measured against Arcane 2.14.0 with one agent; a report from other versions is welcome.
